policy.rule: A candidate disposition controls verification workflow only; it never creates linguistic authority.
policy.closedMeaning: Reviewed and intentionally not published as an independent learner morpheme.
policy.deferredMeaning: Potentially meaningful, but insufficient evidence or product value to publish now.

decisions.reason: Latin pono directly supports PON/PONE/POSIT. POS alone is an arbitrary pedagogical truncation of posui/positum rather than a separately attested source-language morpheme; LexiFlow will teach the evidenced forms instead.
Allen & Greenough explicitly analyzes mitt-i-tis with root MIT and consonant doubling in the present stem. MITT is therefore a stem spelling effect, not a separate root.

Latin misi is part of the mittere paradigm, but publishing learner-facing MIS would collide with the unrelated English/Germanic mis- prefix. MIT/MISS plus the verified MISE transmission provide a safer teaching model.

TIN appears in traditional pedagogical groupings around teneo compounds, but LexiFlow requires a separately documented compound-stem/vowel-change rule before publishing it as an independent teaching form. TEN/TENT authority and TAIN transmission are already available.

Latin authority already has VIV from vivo/vivus. The sequence vivi- is not required as a separate learner morpheme; publishing it would duplicate an inflected/derived surface sequence rather than add a distinct source-language fact.
Lewis & Short explicitly derives vitalis from vita. LexiFlow therefore keeps VITA as the source-language authority form instead of publishing the pedagogical truncation VIT.
Latin pes, pedis directly supports PED as the source-language stem. PEDI is not needed as an independent morpheme record; word-level analysis can link relevant forms back to PED.

Latin pes, pedis directly supports PED. The learner form PEDE is a downstream word-shape/pedagogical variant rather than a separately attested source-language morpheme, so it is intentionally not published.
